```{r}
### create functions for Fig. S1 ###
# Get lower triangle of the correlation matrix
get_lower_tri<-function(cormat){
  cormat[upper.tri(cormat)] <- NA
  return(cormat)
}
# Get upper triangle of the correlation matrix
get_upper_tri <- function(cormat){
  cormat[lower.tri(cormat)]<- NA
  return(cormat)
}

reorder_cormat <- function(cormat){
  dd <- as.dist((1 - cormat) / 2)
  hc <- hclust(dd)
  return(cormat[hc$order, hc$order])  # Return the reordered matrix
}

```

#### Generate Figure S1, correlation matrix of variables associated with the presence of food waste #####

```{r}

#### cor matrix 750. m #####
### explore correlation of variables associated with the presence of food waste ### 


dat_no_ub_no0s <- dat_no_ub %>%
  filter(fw_score_weighted > 0 ) ### 0 equivalent val (minimum fw_score_weighted val after scaling, not to be used as response)

# dat_no_ub_scaled_no0s <- dat_no_ub %>%
#   filter(fw_score_weighted > -0.1632483) ### 0 equivalent val (minimum fw_score_weighted val after scaling, not to be used as response)
# 


my_data <- dat_no_ub_no0s %>% select(where(is.numeric))
#my_data <- dat_no_ub_scaled_no0s %>% select(where(is.numeric))
my_data <- as.data.frame(my_data)

my_data <- my_data[, colSums(is.na(my_data)) == 0]  # Remove NA columns

# Define the variables to keep in the heatmap
selected_vars <- c("rent_pct", "single_detached" ,
                   "nearest_food_retail","nearest_shelter_dist","indig_pct",
                   "female_pct", "SCOREMAT", "SCORESOC", "pop_km",
                   "household_income", "housing_highdensity", "housing_lowdensity",
                   "thirtyonshelter_majorrepairs", "notsuitable_majorrepairs", "pct_rent_subsidized", "pct_housing_notsuitable","pct_rent_thiry", "housing_low_density", "housing_high_density", "poorservice_housing")  # Replace with actual column names



# Ensure the selected variables exist in the dataset
selected_vars <- selected_vars[selected_vars %in% colnames(my_data)]

# Subset data to only include selected variables
my_data_subset <- my_data[, selected_vars]
cormat <- cor(my_data_subset)

cormat <- reorder_cormat(cormat)
lower_tri <- get_lower_tri(cormat)
melted_cormat <- melt(lower_tri)



# # Filter correlations greater than 0.5 (absolute value)
# melted_cormat <- melted_cormat[abs(melted_cormat$value) > 0.5, ]
# melted_cormat <- melted_cormat[complete.cases(melted_cormat), ]

magma_colors <- magma(10)

heatmap <- ggplot(data = melted_cormat, aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(value, 2)), color = "black", size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = magma_colors[7],     # Dark orange (negative correlations)
    mid = "white",              # Neutral zero
    high = magma_colors[3],     # Deep purple (positive correlations)
    midpoint = 0,
    limits = c(-1, 1),
    name = "Pearson R"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1),
    axis.title = element_blank()
  )

ggsave(
  filename = here("figs", "FigureS1.pdf"),
  plot = heatmap,
  device = pdf,
  width = 8,
  height = 7,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 300
)
```


#### Figures S2, S5, S6 and supplementary tables (revised November 2026)

The main model is now **F123_all**: all three socio-political scales (Housing-tenure—density,
Deprivation, Disenfranchisement) in both the presence and quantity parts of the zero-inflated
Weibull model, fit to the corrected 3-factor, 16-variable factor analysis
(`src/factor_analysis_revision.R`). Scales are oriented so that higher values are the less
privileged condition; presence effects are on the log-odds of presence.

`src/supplement_figures_F123_all.R` writes:

- `figs/FigureS2.pdf`: factor-analysis loading biplots (oriented)
- `figs/FigureS5.pdf`: prior predictive simulations for F123_all
- `figs/FigureS6.png`: posterior predictive checks for F123_all
- `tables/Table_factor_loadings.csv`, `tables/Table_F123_all_coefficients.csv`,
  `tables/Table_LOO_all_models.csv`, `tables/Table_bins_litter.csv`,
  `tables/Table_weight_sensitivity.csv`

```{r supplement-F123-all}
source(here("src", "supplement_figures_F123_all.R"), local = new.env())  # own environment: does not overwrite objects used by other chunks
```

The previous Figure S2 code (biplot from the superseded factor-analysis run) has been removed;
see the git history of this file.

#### Figure S7: the three socio-political scales across the City of Vancouver

Revised: corrected city factor scores (transect regression weights and standardization), oriented
so that higher values are the less privileged condition, on a shared diverging scale; DAs with
population density below 650 persons km^-2^ are not shown. Replaces the former S7 and S8
(maps of the superseded Factor 1 and Factor 3 scores).


#### Figure S9

```{r}
library(sf)

#load(file = here("data", "van_dat_final_750_2.Rdata"))

load(file = here("data", "van_dat_demo_lc_retail_shelters_roads_mods_750.Rdata"))

# Load site polygons
load(here("data", "sites_3857.Rdata"))
sites_3857 <- sites_3857[-c(8),]  # Remove one site if needed



# Site labels (must match order in sites_matched)
site_labels <- c(
  "Collingwood", "McKenzie", "Shaugnessy", "Queen Elizabeth",
  "False Creek", "Downtown", "West End", "43 & Churchill",
  "14 & Spruce", "19 & Yukon", "Strathcona", "2nd Beach"
)

# Get site centroids
site_centroids <- st_centroid(sites_3857)
label_coords <- st_coordinates(site_centroids)

# ---- AUTO-NUDGE: Spread labels based on position ----

# bottom of map (y-axis)
bottom_y <- min(label_coords[,2]) - 500  # 500 m below the lowest site
center_x <- mean(label_coords[,1])       # horizontally centered

# new center for label push
label_center <- c(center_x, bottom_y)

# direction vectors
dx <- label_coords[,1] - label_center[1]
dy <- label_coords[,2] - label_center[2]

# normalize
dist <- sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2)
dx_norm <- dx / dist
dy_norm <- dy / dist

# simple, consistent push
push_dist <- 1000   # <- tune this (200–500 is the sweet spot)

label_coords_offset <- label_coords
label_coords_offset[,1] <- label_coords[,1] + dx_norm * push_dist
label_coords_offset[,2] <- label_coords[,2] + dy_norm * push_dist
# find indices
i_col <- which(site_labels == "Collingwood")
i_mck <- which(site_labels == "McKenzie")

# vertical separation (strong + clean)
label_coords_offset[i_col,2] <- label_coords_offset[i_col,2] + 120
label_coords_offset[i_mck,2] <- label_coords_offset[i_mck,2] + 300

label_coords_offset[i_col,1] <- label_coords_offset[i_col,1] - 120
label_coords_offset[i_mck,1] <- label_coords_offset[i_mck,1] + 300

# Convert to data frame and attach labels
label_df <- as.data.frame(label_coords_offset)
colnames(label_df) <- c("X", "Y")
label_df$label <- site_labels

# Offsets for 8-direction outline
offsets <- expand.grid(dx = c(-0.5, 0, 0.5),
                       dy = c(-0.5, 0, 0.5))
offsets <- offsets[!(offsets$dx == 0 & offsets$dy == 0), ]

# Duplicate label data for outline
outline_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(1:nrow(offsets), function(i) {
  transform(label_df,
            X = X + offsets$dx[i],
            Y = Y + offsets$dy[i])
}))


# Define output file name and resolution
pdf(here("figs","FigureS9.pdf"), width = 10, height = 8)

ggplot() +
  # Base raster/grid layer
  geom_sf(data = van_dat, aes(fill = housing_highdensity), color = NA) +

  # Site polygons
  geom_sf(data = sites_3857, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 1.75) +
  geom_sf(data = sites_3857, fill = NA, color = "white", linewidth = 0.75) +
# Outline
geom_text(
  data = outline_df,
  aes(x = X, y = Y, label = label),
  size = 4.1,
  fontface = "bold",
  color = "black"
) +

# Foreground
geom_text(
  data = label_df,
  aes(x = X, y = Y, label = label),
  size = 4,
  fontface = "bold",
  color = "white"
)+
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "viridis",
    name = "High-density \nHousing"
  ) +

  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
    legend.text  = element_text(size = 10)
  )

dev.off()
```

#### Figure S15: posterior predictive checks of the proxy (Tweedie) model
```{r}

load( file = here("data","fit_hier_1pred_tweedie.Rdata"))
# Extract samples
posterior <- rstan::extract(fit_hier_1pred_tweedie)

# Extract posterior samples
y_rep <- posterior$y_rep  # Change "y_rep" based on how you named your predicted values
y_obs <- dat_no_ub$fw_score_weighted  # Replace with actual observed data
pi_obs <- ifelse(dat_no_ub$fw_score_weighted > 0 , 0, 1)  # Convert to binary presence/absence
# Flatten it first (if you want to look across all draws)
y_rep_pos <- as.vector(y_rep)
y_rep_pos <- y_rep_pos[y_rep_pos > 0]



# Explore distributions
hist(posterior$mu, breaks = 40, main = "mu", col = "skyblue")
hist(posterior$phi, breaks = 40, main = "alpha", col = "salmon")
hist(posterior$p, breaks = 40, main = "log_scale", col = "salmon")
hist(posterior$lambda, breaks = 40, main = "sigma", col = "salmon")
hist(posterior$eta, breaks = 40, main = "sigma", col = "salmon")
hist(posterior$beta1, breaks = 40, main = "beta1", col = "pink")

set.seed(123)  # for reproducibility
sample_rows <- sample(1:nrow(y_rep), 50)  # randomly pick 50 rows


# ppc_dens_overlay(y_obs, y_rep[sample_rows,])  # Plot overlay of observed vs simulated densities
# 
# 
# 
# # Plot overlay of observed vs simulated densities with x-axis range 0 to 4
# ppc_dens_overlay(y_obs, y_rep[sample_rows, ]) +
#  # xlim(0.000001,10) +
#   labs(title = "Posterior Predictive Check (Full Range)",
#        x = "Food Waste Score",
#        y = "Density") +
#   theme_minimal()
# 
# 
# # Plot overlay of observed vs simulated densities with x-axis range 0 to 4
# ppc_dens_overlay(y_obs, y_rep[sample_rows, ]) +
#   xlim(0.000001,10) +
#   labs(title = "Posterior Predictive Check (X Range: >0 to 10)",
#        x = "Food Waste Score",
#        y = "Density") +
#   theme_minimal()
# 
# 
# # Plot overlay of observed vs simulated densities with x-axis range 0 to 4
# ppc_dens_overlay(y_obs, y_rep[sample_rows, ]) +
#   xlim(-0.01,1) +
#   labs(title = "Posterior Predictive Check (X Range: 0 to 2.5)",
#        x = "Food Waste Score",
#        y = "Density") +
#   theme_minimal()

# Draw subset of posterior predictive simulations
sample_rows <- sample(nrow(y_rep), 50)

base_theme <- theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "none"
  )

# Create a separate plot solely for extracting the legend
legend_plot <- ppc_dens_overlay(
  y_obs,
  y_rep[sample_rows, ]
) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

shared_legend <- get_legend(legend_plot)


# Panel A: full range
p1 <- ppc_dens_overlay(
  y_obs,
  y_rep[sample_rows, ]
) +
  labs(
    title = "Full Range",
    x = "",
    y = "Density"
  ) +
  base_theme

# Panel B: zoom to 0-10
p2 <- ppc_dens_overlay(
  y_obs,
  y_rep[sample_rows, ]
) +
  xlim(0.000001,10) +
  labs(
    title = "Zoom: >0–10",
    x = "",
    y = ""
  )  +
  base_theme

# Panel C: zoom near zero
p3 <- ppc_dens_overlay(
  y_obs,
  y_rep[sample_rows, ]
) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.01, 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Zoom: 0–1",
    x = "",
    y = ""
  ) +
  base_theme


# Combine panels
panel_row <- plot_grid(
  p1, p2, p3,
  labels = c("a", "b", "c"),
  ncol = 3,
  align = "hv",
  axis = "tblr",
  label_size = 16
)

# Shared x-axis
x_label <- ggdraw() +
  draw_label(
    "Food Waste Score",
    size = 14
  )

# Panels + x-axis
main_plot <- plot_grid(
  panel_row,
  x_label,
  ncol = 1,
  rel_heights = c(1, 0.08)
)

# Add legend on the right
plot_grid(
  main_plot,
  shared_legend,
  ncol = 2,
  rel_widths = c(1, 0.15)
)


final_plot <- plot_grid(
  main_plot,
  shared_legend,
  ncol = 2,
  rel_widths = c(1, 0.12)
)

# Display
print(final_plot)

# Save wide version
ggsave(
  here("figs","FigureS15.png"),
  final_plot,
  width = 12,
  height = 4,
  dpi = 300
)
```
